claims.claim: DO Penedès is a Mediterranean wine area in Catalonia, southwest of Barcelona. Its vineyards run from near sea level to about 800 m inland.
claims.note: Guía Peñín gives up to 800 m for Upper Penedès. The DO page gives no top altitude but notes vineyards above 600 m get more rain and wider day-night swings.

claims.claim: The traditional three-way split is Baix Penedès (Penedès Marítim, near the sea), Penedès Central or Mitjà (the plain between), and Alt Penedès (Penedès Superior, inland against the mountains).
claims.note: Official older site calls them Marítim, Central and Superior. Guía Peñín says Lower, Middle or Central, and Upper. The word Mitjà is the Catalan for middle and is not used on the pages read.

claims.claim: Baix Penedès is the lowest and warmest zone because of the sea. Alt Penedès is the highest and coolest, with bigger day-night swings, more frost and more rain. The Central zone mixes both climates and, in Guía Peñín's account, supplies much of the grapes for cava.
claims.quote: The Lower Penedès is warmer because of the sea's influence.

claims.claim: Parellada is the traditional grape of the cooler, high Alt Penedès. Xarel·lo and Macabeo dominate the Central zone, where much goes into cava.

Today the DO also uses a 2015 soil-based subzone map with around ten zones, such as Marina del Garraf, Costers del Montmell, Alts d'Ancosa and Massís del Garraf i Costers de l'Ordal. The older three-zone split is no longer how the DO describes itself.
claims.note: The 2015 note names seven zones, the current site lists ten. Rules for labelling by subzone were not confirmed as finalised.

claims.claim: Overall climate is Mediterranean, mild and warm. Zone average temperatures run from about 11-14 C in Alts d'Ancosa (coldest) to 16-17 C on the Garraf coast (warmest). Rain runs from about 500 mm on the coast to about 650 mm inland.

Soils vary by zone. Common types are shallow young soils on steep slopes, deeper soils on gentle slopes and valley floors, and calcium carbonate build-up. Parent rocks include Cretaceous limestone, marl and dolomite (Garraf and Ordal), slate and granite (Anoia hillsides) and sandstone and marl (Lavernó hillsides).

The DO specification names three geological units: the Garraf Massif, the pre-coastal Penedès Depression, and the inland mountain range between Montserrat and the Montmell. Low ground has Miocene sandstone and marl from alluvial fans at the foot of the mountains.
claims.note: Read through a search summary of the PDF, not the PDF text.

claims.claim: Guía Peñín describes Penedès soils as deep and permeable, a balance of sand and clay, poor in organic matter and not very fertile.
Montserrat is the jagged mountain to the north of the Penedès. The DO specification uses it as one end of the inland range (Montserrat to Montmell) that frames the Penedès basin.
claims.note: Only the geological mention is sourced. No source found on Montserrat's effect on the vineyards, and the DO climate page does not mention it.

claims.claim: DO Cava is not tied to one place. Official zones are Comtats de Barcelona, Valle del Ebro, Viñedos de Almendralejo and Requena (Levante). The Barcelona zone is Catalan Cava and has five subzones: Valls d'Anoia-Foix, Serra de Mar, Conca del Gaià, Serra de Prades and Pla de Ponent. The Ebro zone has Alto Ebro and Valle del Cierzo.
claims.note: Sub-zones approved in 2020. The Levante zone is called Requena on the Consejo's zones page and was unnamed in the BOE news item.

claims.claim: The Consejo Regulador says Cava began in the Penedès, especially in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia and around it, and calls the town the capital of Cava.
claims.quote: The origins of Cava lie in the winemaking area of Penedés, especially in the town of San Sadurní d'Anoia

claims.claim: Nearly all Cava is made in Catalonia, mostly in the Penedès, and Sant Sadurní d'Anoia alone is said to make most of it. Reported figures are more than 90 to 95% from the Penedès and over 75% from Sant Sadurní.
claims.note: Figures come from secondary pages and search snippets, not the Consejo's statistics. Use the wording 'most' on a sheet, not a number.

claims.claim: Cava de Guarda Superior (Reserva, Gran Reserva, Paraje Calificado) has stricter rules: organic grapes, vines older than 10 years, and a maximum yield of 10,000 kg/ha. Organic was to be mandatory by 2025.
claims.note: Check the date for the organic rule before printing it.

claims.claim: Cava is made by the traditional method. The base wine is bottled with yeast and sugar, a second fermentation happens in the bottle, and the wine then ages on its lees.
claims.quote: differentiated from other systems by a second fermentation in the bottle

claims.claim: Nine grapes are authorised. White: Macabeo, Xarel·lo, Parellada, Chardonnay, Subirat Parent. Red: Garnacha, Trepat, Monastrell, Pinot Noir. Macabeo is the most planted, then Xarel·lo, then Parellada. Together those three are the classic Cava blend.
Cava (Cava de Guarda) must age at least 9 months on the lees.
Reserva needs at least 18 months of ageing. It is part of Cava de Guarda Superior.
claims.note: The BOE news item also mentions a 15 to 18 month change. The Consejo's own pages say 18.

claims.claim: Gran Reserva needs at least 30 months of ageing.
claims.note: The Consejo news page that states 30 is clear. A second Consejo page did not give the figure.

claims.claim: Paraje Calificado needs at least 36 months of ageing, and comes from a single named plot and estate-made wine that passes a tasting committee.
claims.note: 36 months seen in the BOE item and the infographic summary. The committee detail is from a search summary.

claims.claim: The Consejo and press describe these as time in the bottle, and the lees contact is the same period. Counted from tirage (bottling for second fermentation).
claims.note: Official pages say 'ageing in the bottle'. Counting from tirage is standard but was not confirmed in text read.

conflicts: Zones: the user brief, Guía Peñín and the older DO site use three zones (Baix, Mitjà/Central, Alt/Superior). The current DO site lists ten soil-based zones. The 2015 note says seven. Both can be true, since the three-way split is a general geography.
Cava Levante zone is called Requena on the Consejo's zones page, unnamed in the BOE news item, and one source lists only three zones.
Reserva is 18 months on the Consejo pages, but the BOE news item also says 15 to 18 months.
gaps: No source found for where the name Penedès comes from. Do not state an etymology.
No source on the origin of the word Cava (cellar) was read. Do not state it.
Montserrat's own influence on climate and soil was not found. Only the geological mention in the specification.

sheet.place: Penedès sits southwest of Barcelona, from the sea up to about 800 m inland. The climate is warm and Mediterranean, and the soils are limestone, marl and sandstone.
sheet.rules: Cava is made by the traditional method, with a second fermentation in the bottle. Cava needs 9 months on the lees, Reserva 18, Gran Reserva 30 and Paraje Calificado 36. Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada are the classic grapes.
